newsitem.title: GERMANY: Plug tax holes with privatisations-German industry.
newsitem.headline: Plug tax holes with privatisations-German industry.

text.p: The head of the Federation of German Industry (BDI) on Thursday called for an increased privatisation drive to boost state funds in the light of Germany's estimated 18 billion mark ($10.6 billion) 1997 tax shortfall.
"The federal state has already done its bit as much as possible," BDI chief Hans-Olaf Henkel said in a statement.
"But there are literally thousands of companies still in the hands of the regional states and communes, many of which are obvious privatisation candidates," he added.

Henkel also called for a round of public cost-cutting, aimed at Germany's "over-flowing welfare budget" and not at areas such as training, research and development which he said were crucial to economic growth.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel provoked controversy on Wednesday when he said the government was considering selling some of its remaining stake in the telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom earlier than initially envisaged.
